newsitem.title: UK: Portugal plans golden share in EDP - Franco.
newsitem.headline: Portugal plans golden share in EDP - Franco.

text.p: Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Wednesday the planned privatisation of state electricity company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal would involve a "golden share" for the government.
"At this moment we think it will be necessary," Franco said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV), due to be broadcast later on Wednesday.
"First there will be a minority privatisation, then a majority with a golden share," he said.
He also said the privatisation "base" would be at least 25 percent but that that was flexible.
The privatisation, which is set to become the biggest ever carried out in Portugal, could be for as much as 49 percent, a Portuguese official told Reuters in early March.
"We think we'll be far away from the (maximum amount) which the law allows us to privatise," Franco said on Wednesday.
A golden share is generally a stake in a company which allows the holder to maintain a degree of power, typically achieved by allowing sufficient voting rights.
Last week Portugal's State Secretary for Industry and Energy Jose Penedos said the sale could slip from mid-May to June in order to avoid a clash with the planned float of France Telecom.
Asked about the timing of the third phase of privatisation of Portugal Telecom, Franco said it would be "still this year, but later on, the second semester."
"But it depends on market conditions," he added.
